target_customer: Businesses, marketing and sales teams that host, share and track video
problem: Companies embedded YouTube videos that showed rivals' ads and gave little analytics, while enterprise video platforms like Ooyala and Brightcove were costly.
business_model: SaaS subscription, freemium at launch (20 to 50 dollars a month premium), later enterprise sales and sales video tools
product_category: Business video hosting, analytics and sales video platform

founders.name: Michael Litt
education: University of Waterloo, Systems Design Engineering
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; Redwoods Media from the Vidyard about page.

founders.name: Devon Galloway
founders.background_notes: From the YC page and the company about page, which says the two met at Waterloo.

competitors.name: Ooyala
competitors.what: Enterprise hosted video platform described as expensive

competitors.name: Brightcove
competitors.what: Enterprise hosted video platform described as expensive

competitors.name: YouTube
competitors.what: Free video hosting that businesses embedded on their sites; Litt cited 3.5 million businesses doing so
competitors.traction_then: 3.5 million businesses embedding videos, per the founder

technical_complexity.rationale: Video hosting, branded players, real time analytics and syndication needed streaming and analytics work, but used commodity cloud components.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded players, viewer analytics and CRM integrations create lock in, but Wistia, Vimeo and Brightcove remained viable alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it into oblivion or acquired it; Vidyard acquired Switch Merge in 2015 and is still independent.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2011 cited 3.5 million businesses embedding YouTube videos on their sites, the problem of competitor ads and related videos, and the high cost of enterprise platforms. Early customers included Ernst and Young and Adchemy.

identity.logo: Emblem with the V-Bot character paired with a wordmark, per a third party brand guidelines summary
identity.mascot_or_character: V-Bot, a friendly robot (third party summary, not confirmed on the company site)
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline Video for every customer moment; helps revenue teams scale trust

rebrands.why: To focus exclusively on video sales and marketing technology, per the Vidyard about page

branding.community_and_virality: Vidyard was featured in The Verge's Small Empires series per its about page; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in B2B video with a mascot and media features, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.from: Redwoods Media, a video production company that also offered hosting and analytics
pivots.to: Vidyard, a video hosting and analytics software product
pivots.why: To focus exclusively on video sales and marketing technology, per the company about page

outcome_analysis: Vidyard started as a freemium YouTube alternative for businesses, raised a seed round in November 2011 and Series A through C by January 2016 (6, 18 and 35 million), then moved toward enterprise and sales video. It is cash flow profitable according to the CEO in a Logic article and reached about 91 million dollars raised by April 2024. It cut about 20 percent of staff in 2023 amid broader tech layoffs and remains independent.
notes: Series A amount and date come from aggregators (Sacra and others) and the lead is disputed (OMERS in one, SoftTech and Jill Rowley in another); Vidyard's own Series B release confirms a Series A with OMERS but gives no amount. The seed amount comes from a TechCrunch headline seen in search results (page not opened); the TechCrunch launch article names the Start Fund, Y Combinator, SV Angel and Dennis Kavelman with no amounts. The 2019 BMO debt facility rests on Bouncewatch alone. The 2024 round is 15M per Sacra and 21M per Bouncewatch, labeled Series D by CB Insights, so it rests on aggregators; Sacra total about 91M matches the rounds recorded. Layoffs of about 20 percent in 2023 come from a law firm blog and TrueUp. The V-Bot mascot comes from a third party guidelines summary not opened. Name origin of Vidyard not found.
